title: Enterprise Security and RBAC Governance Layer
summary: Enforce least-privilege tenant/project-scoped role and policy decisions across every AGASTYA enforcement point.

intent.statement: Govern all protected actions through authenticated identity, exact scope, role/capability, context, policy version and evidence-backed decision.
desired_outcomes: No protected action defaults to allow.
Enterprise roles are scoped, time-bound and non-escalating.
Policy decisions remain reproducible and auditable.

success_measures.name: PEP coverage
success_measures.target: 100% protected API, worker, agent, extension, Vault and streaming actions evaluate policy
success_measures.measurement_method: Reconcile protected operation registry with policy decision evidence.

problem.statement: Static roles alone cannot govern tenant/project isolation, privileged actions, agent/service access, policy change and separation of duties across AGASTYA runtimes.
problem.current_state: Platform specifications have local policy controls but no unified enterprise identity/capability/policy lifecycle.
impact: Privilege escalation or conflicted approvals could occur.
Historic decisions may lack policy provenance.

business_context.business_value: A common enterprise policy layer lets AGASTYA scale safely from project access to autonomous tools and evidence-backed operations.

actors.name: Policy Enforcement Point
goals: Allow, deny or gate protected actions.

actors.name: Agent Identity
goals: Act only under exact task/project capability.

functional_requirements.title: Map enterprise identities
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall map authenticated humans, groups, services, agents and break-glass identities to tenant-scoped identity records and assurance attributes.

functional_requirements.title: Manage scoped role grants
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall define versioned role/capability bundles and scope-bound assignments with grantor, purpose, start, expiry, review and revocation metadata.

functional_requirements.title: Evaluate policy at every PEP
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall evaluate policy before every protected API, CLI, worker, agent, extension, Vault and streaming operation.

functional_requirements.title: Enforce separation of duties
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall prevent conflicted self-approval, self-escalation and prohibited policy/approval combinations.

functional_requirements.title: Govern privileged and non-human access
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall require step-up and JIT approval for configured privileged actions and issue only narrow expiring non-human grants to registered workloads, agents and tools.

functional_requirements.title: Version policies and evidence
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall version, simulate/test, approve, activate, supersede and roll back policy while retaining policy decision provenance and Ledger evidence.

non_functional_requirements.statement: Missing, stale, ambiguous or denied identity/scope/policy facts shall result in deny or required approval, never implicit allow.
non_functional_requirements.verification_method: Negative enforcement tests remove one required decision fact per PEP.
non_functional_requirements.target: No protected action succeeds under incomplete policy context.

business_rules.statement: A grant cannot exceed the grantor's delegable authority and must carry tenant/project scope, purpose, start and expiry.
Each protected action requires a versioned ALLOW, DENY or WAITING_APPROVAL policy decision before execution.
A subject may not approve its own governed change or approve a prohibited conflicted role/policy action.

constraints.statement: Initial governance is deny-by-default and does not enable specific SSO, SCIM, production policy engine, break-glass or customer-directory integration until their child contracts are approved.
constraints.rationale: Identity and privileged access require explicit architecture/security decisions.

dependencies.name: Enterprise identity and policy provider
dependencies.risk: Identity claims, session revocation and policy evaluation architecture are pending.

bounded_contexts.name: Identity Access and Governance
bounded_contexts.responsibility: Own identities, roles, assignments, capabilities, policy decisions, separation rules and privileged grants.

ubiquitous_language.definition: Allowed action after identity, scope, role, context, policy and approval evaluation.
Runtime boundary that must enforce PDP decision before protected action.

workflows.name: Evaluate protected action
workflows.trigger: Human or workload requests protected operation.

steps.action: Resolves identity, assurance, scope, role, resource, environment, policy and approval facts.
steps.result: Versioned ALLOW, DENY or WAITING_APPROVAL decision.
Action executes minimally or is blocked/gated.

steps.action: Writes metadata-only decision and outcome evidence.

security_requirements.statement: Every policy enforcement point shall perform tenant/project scope, role/capability and contextual policy evaluation before protected action and emit safe decision evidence.
security_requirements.verification_method: Cross-PEP security suite tests API, worker, agent, extension, Vault and streaming denial/gate paths.

observability_requirements.statement: Policy, role/grant, privileged access, denial, revocation and simulation lifecycle shall emit correlated Ledger evidence.
observability_requirements.verification_method: Reconstruct policy decision and historic policy version from audit evidence.

acceptance_criteria.title: Scoped read enforces policy
acceptance_criteria.when: It reads allowed and disallowed classified resources.
acceptance_criteria.then: Policy allows only permitted read and denies safely otherwise.

acceptance_criteria.title: Self approval is blocked
acceptance_criteria.then: Separation policy denies and records evidence.

acceptance_criteria.title: Delegation cannot escalate
acceptance_criteria.then: It is denied without privilege escalation.

acceptance_criteria.title: Privileged action waits for assurance
acceptance_criteria.then: Action is denied or waits before sensitive step.

acceptance_criteria.title: Nonhuman grant stays narrow
acceptance_criteria.then: It gets only narrow expiring grant or denial.

acceptance_criteria.title: Policy history remains reproducible
acceptance_criteria.given: Proposed policy has simulation and approval.
acceptance_criteria.then: Evidence records version and historic decisions retain prior policy provenance.

test_requirements.scope: Role scope, delegation and separation-of-duties enforcement.
JIT privileged and non-human grant controls.

risks.title: Inconsistent PEP enforcement or privileged role misuse
risks.description: A bypassed PEP or overbroad role could undermine all platform controls.
risks.mitigation: Deny-by-default PEP contract, policy coverage tests, JIT access and Ledger evidence.

open_questions.question: Which federated identity provider, MFA/step-up claims and session/revocation model apply?
open_questions.impact_if_unresolved: Identity and assurance integration cannot be implemented.
open_questions.resolution: Accepted as a detailed-design risk. Federated identity, step-up claims and session-revocation architecture is mandatory before implementation.

open_questions.question: Which policy expression/evaluation technology meets explainability, versioning and test requirements?
open_questions.impact_if_unresolved: Enterprise PDP/PEP implementation cannot be selected.
open_questions.resolution: Accepted as a detailed-design risk. Policy expression/evaluation technology ADR is mandatory before PEP implementation.

architecture_decisions.title: Use RBAC with contextual policy enforcement at every protected runtime boundary
architecture_decisions.context: Static roles alone cannot govern resource classification, environment, task purpose, approval and agent/service access.
architecture_decisions.decision: Assign scoped role/capability bundles and require policy decision at API, worker, agent, extension, Vault and streaming enforcement points.

alternatives.name: Role checks embedded independently in each service
alternatives.rejection_reason: Creates inconsistent policy, weak audit provenance and bypass risk.

architecture_decisions.rationale: Central versioned decision model plus distributed enforcement preserves least privilege and reconstructable evidence.
consequences: Identity and policy engine architecture must be selected.

provenance.rationale: Enterprise governance extends project isolation and role boundary.

coverage_summary.method: Initial governance draft mapping; implementation coverage is not yet applicable.

change_history.summary: Initial Enterprise Security and RBAC Governance Layer draft.
change_history.reason: Define cross-platform policy and role governance before selecting enterprise identity/policy technologies.

change_history.summary: Enterprise Security and RBAC Governance Layer approved for detailed design.
change_history.reason: The Project Sponsor approved the deny-by-default enterprise policy model.

approvals.reason: Approved by the Project Sponsor for detailed governance design subject to identity and policy-engine gates.
